messages:
karen: FYI we got a high-severity report from a customer experiencing intermittent 5xx/504s during a traffic burst. they reported SDK retry loops and an unexplained billing spike. attaching the snippets they sent.

karen: ```
RequestId: r-0a1b2c3d
HTTP/2 504
upstream timed out (110) while reading response header from upstream
SDK: retrying request, attempt=4, backoff=200ms
embedding.size=64
num_concurrent=450
```

ian: ack. thanks. can we reproduce internally? need exact client pattern (concurrency, keepalive, http2 vs http1). asked customer for SDK version and whether they use connection pooling.

karen: they said node SDK v1.6.2 with default pool. concurrency ~400-500 short-lived requests, mostly streaming completion endpoints.

maya: initial hypothesis: edge proxy/workload is starving ephemeral ports or connection reuse is poor -> many half-open/orphaned conns causing head-of-line and upstream timeouts. also possible idle keepalive ttl mismatch between edge and upstream. i can try to repro with a small load script.

samir: quick check: pulled edge proxy logs around that window, seeing a pattern of FIN_WAIT/RESET spikes. excerpt: ```
2024-03-09T21:12:03Z edge-proxy[connmgr]: conn 0x7f8 -> backend reset (RST) after 29s
2024-03-09T21:12:04Z edge-proxy[connmgr]: conn 0x6a2 orphaned, no activity for 12s, reaped
```

samir: also saw many 502/504 -> `upstream send-timeout` entries. putting metrics on a dashboard now.

maya: repro plan: simulate 500 concurrent clients opening HTTP/2 streams with short-lived calls and deliberately disable connection reuse on client to mimic their pattern. command i used:```
# quick repro (wrk2-like)
for i in {1..500}; do node repro/stream_burst.js &
done
```
where repro/stream_burst.js opens new HTTP/2 connection, sends one streaming completion, then closes.

ian: run that against staging edge and capture: kernel netstat, proxy conn counts, NAT table metrics (if any). if we see SNAT port exhaustion we can correlate.

maya: ran it on staging. observed transient 504s after ~60s. kernel shows many sockets in TIME_WAIT and a large ephemeral port reuse rate. logs:```
netstat -an | grep 197.251.1.2:443 | wc -l
> 620
```
proxy threads: open fds nearing soft limit on one box.

samir: looks like both connection churn and proxy FD exhaustion. possible contributing factor: upstream keepalive_timeout shorter than proxy->upstream idle reuse, causing more reconnects.

ian: immediate mitigation options?

maya: proposed mitigations (short-term):
- increase per-proxy FD/u limits and connection_backlog temporarily
- tune keepalive on proxy to match upstream (increase to 120s)
- enable connection reuse in SDK (recommend customer upgrade to sdk v1.7.0 which enables persistent pooled connections by default)
- add small token-bucket at ingress for per-customer concurrency to avoid burst stomping the edge

samir: operational steps I'm taking now: bump ulimit on 3 edge hosts, restart proxy workers gracefully (rolling) to reclaim FD leaks, and add a temporary NAT pool expansion in the egress gateway. deploy-bot: scheduling rolling restart.

deploy-bot: scheduled rolling restart for edge-proxy cluster edge-prod-1 at 2024-03-10T02:15:00Z (UTC). will restart one host at a time.

ops-bot: increased ephemeral port range on egress nodes and applied new sysctl: net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 15000 61000

karen: communicated to customer: "we're investigating, short-term mitigation rolling out (edge restarts + sysctl). please hold on further debugging while we run these steps. recommend enabling connection pooling client-side in meantime." :white_check_mark:

ian: after mitigation we should monitor: 5xx rate per-customer, socket FD usage, SYN backlog, and any billing anomalies tied to retries. also add temporary alert for connection churn.

maya: post mitigation results: 5xx rate dropped from 1.8% -> 0.12% in 20m window. FD usage returned to baseline. still watching for any residual retry loops from clients.

karen: customer update: "We've applied a mitigative fix (edge restarts, config tweak) and are monitoring. Please upgrade to SDK v1.7.0 and enable pooling; we'll follow up with root cause and long-term fix."

samir: long-term fixes suggested:
- implement per-customer concurrency backpressure at edge (soft queueing)
- improve connection reuse heuristics and increase connection pool sharing for streaming endpoints
- add server-side circuit breaker signals to instruct SDKs to slow down (429/Retry-After) before 5xx cascades
- postmortem and capacity sizing for peak bursts; consider autoscaling policy adjustments for short burst spikes

ian: creating P1 ticket for postmortem + implementation items. assigned to eng-sre + devex for SDK changes.

karen: customer acknowledged and said they'll test SDK upgrade next week. will keep thread updated.

maya: note for the PMs: quantifying cost/billing impact from retry loops is important; the billing team should look at token counts correlated with retry window.

ian: closing loop internally once postmortem doc is ready. thanks all for fast triage. :pray:

samir: small note — add regression test in our integration suite to simulate high-churn short-lived connection bursts so we don't regress this.

karen: marking as solved for customer for now; will reopen if they see more.

ian: moving to follow-up board, leaving thread here for records.
